title: Graded prime avoidance
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring [def-pc-proj] (so $S_aS_b\subseteq S_{a+b}$; elements of $S_n$ are homogeneous of degree $n$; an ideal is graded, or homogeneous, if it contains the homogeneous components of each of its elements; $S_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}S_n$), let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r$ be homogeneous prime ideals, and let $I\subseteq S_+$ be a graded ideal not contained in any $\mathfrak p_i$. Then there is a homogeneous element $x\in I$ of positive degree such that $x\notin\mathfrak p_i$ for every $i$.

proof.text: By deleting any $\mathfrak p_j$ that is contained in another $\mathfrak p_i$, we may assume that no inclusion $\mathfrak p_i\subseteq\mathfrak p_j$ holds for distinct indices: avoiding the larger prime automatically avoids the smaller one, so the conclusion for the reduced list implies the original conclusion.

We argue by induction on $r$. For $r=1$, choose a nonzero homogeneous component of an element of $I$ that is outside $\mathfrak p_1$. Such a component exists because $I$ is graded, $\mathfrak p_1$ is homogeneous, and $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_1$; since $I\subseteq S_+$, the component has positive degree. It lies in $I$ and outside $\mathfrak p_1$.

source.place: Algebra Lemma 00JS, proof, the case r=1

proof.text: For the induction step, apply the induction hypothesis to obtain a homogeneous $x\in I$ of positive degree with $x\notin\mathfrak p_i$ for $i<r$. If $x\notin\mathfrak p_r$, it is the required element. Otherwise $x\in\mathfrak p_r$.

Assume $x\in\mathfrak p_r$. The product ideal $I\mathfrak p_1\cdots\mathfrak p_{r-1}$ is not contained in $\mathfrak p_r$: if it were, choose for each $i<r$ an element $a_i\in\mathfrak p_i\setminus\mathfrak p_r$, which is possible because the primes are pairwise non-contained; then for every $z\in I$, $z a_1\cdots a_{r-1}\in\mathfrak p_r$, and primality of $\mathfrak p_r$ together with $a_1\cdots a_{r-1}\notin\mathfrak p_r$ forces $z\in\mathfrak p_r$, contradicting $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_r$.

source.place: Algebra Lemma 00JS, proof, paragraph beginning "If I p_1 ... p_{r-1} subset p_r"

proof.text:
Choose a homogeneous $y\in I\mathfrak p_1\cdots\mathfrak p_{r-1}$ with $y
otin\mathfrak p_r$. The product ideal is graded, so such a $y$ may be chosen homogeneous; because $I\subseteq S_+$, its degree is positive. Put $z=x^{\deg(y)}+y^{\deg(x)}$. Both summands have the same positive degree, so $z$ is homogeneous of positive degree. Since $x\in I$ and $y\in I\mathfrak p_1\cdots\mathfrak p_{r-1}\subseteq I$, $z\in I$. For $i<r$, $y\in\mathfrak p_i$ and $x
otin\mathfrak p_i$, so primality gives $x^{\deg(y)}
otin\mathfrak p_i$ and hence $z
otin\mathfrak p_i$. For $i=r$, $x\in\mathfrak p_r$ and $y
otin\mathfrak p_r$, so $y^{\deg(x)}
otin\mathfrak p_r$ and hence $z
otin\mathfrak p_r$. Thus $z$ has the required property.
